hero.label: FOOD OF THE GODS
hero.subtitle: Food of the Gods
hero.tagline: A chance seedling from British Columbia, named after the mythical food that granted immortality.
origin.label: ORIGIN STORY
origin.title: The Chance Seedling
origin.story: In the early 1990s, in the sun-drenched Similkameen Valley of British Columbia, Canada, the Mennell family noticed something unusual growing among their orchard rows. A chance seedling — neither planted nor planned — had sprung up on its own, bearing fruit unlike any they had seen before. Wilfrid Mennell, struck by the apple's honeyed sweetness and juicy crunch, named it 'Ambrosia' — the food of the gods from Greek mythology. Pickers in the orchard, who seldom eat apples while working, loved the fruit so much they stripped the tree bare before the rest of the harvest was ready. It was a born star.
origin.quote: “Pickers, who seldom eat apples, loved Ambrosia, and stripped the tree before the rest of the orchard was ready.”
timeline.label: TIMELINE
timeline.title: A Journey
timeline.1980s_desc: A mysterious seedling appears in the Mennell family orchard in Cawston, British Columbia.
timeline.1990s_desc: Wilfrid Mennell names the apple 'Ambrosia' after the food of the gods.
timeline.2000s_desc: Ambrosia is propagated as a premium 'club variety' with strict quality controls.
timeline.2015_desc: The Canadian patent expires, allowing broader cultivation.
timeline.2017_desc: American growers gain freedom to cultivate.
timeline.2021_desc: Chilean patent expires. Still active elsewhere until 2034.
timeline.2024_desc: Ambrosia becomes one of the most-produced apple varieties in Canada.
characteristics.label: THE APPLE
characteristics.title: Meet Ambrosia
characteristics.appearance_desc: Bi-colored with glossy red over creamy yellow. Distinctive conical shape.
characteristics.size_desc: Medium to large, 6.8–7.5 cm in diameter, averaging 215 grams.
characteristics.taste_desc: Honeyed sweetness with low acidity. Flavor notes reminiscent of pear.
characteristics.texture_desc: Cream-colored flesh that is firm, crisp, and satisfyingly juicy.
characteristics.browning_desc: Resists oxidation remarkably well — stays fresh-looking in salads.
characteristics.ethylene_desc: Produces very little ethylene, ripens slowly and stores longer.
mythology.label: MYTHOLOGY
mythology.title: Food of the Gods
mythology.body: In ancient Greek mythology, ambrosia was the food of the Olympians, associated with longevity and immortality. When Wilfrid Mennell tasted the apple that had mysteriously appeared in his orchard, its honeyed sweetness evoked this ancient myth.
mythology.quote: As the sapling grew, it bore a few beautiful apples. Wilfrid named it Ambrosia — food of the gods — for its honeyed sweetness and juicy crunch!
parentage.label: PARENTAGE
parentage.title: Bloodline
parentage.intro: Ambrosia was a chance seedling, but it grew in an orchard of giants.

culinary.label: CULINARY
culinary.title: How To Enjoy
culinary.fresh_desc: The ideal snacking apple — sweet, low acid, and the satisfying crunch makes every bite a pleasure.
culinary.salads_desc: Resists browning better than almost any other variety. Stays beautiful in salads for hours.
culinary.baking_desc: Holds its shape under heat. Excellent for pies, tarts, and baked desserts.
culinary.cider_desc: The honeyed sweetness translates beautifully into fresh juice and artisanal ciders.
culinary.cheese_desc: Pairs exceptionally well with aged cheddar, creamy brie, and sharp blue cheeses.
gold.label: PREMIUM TIER
gold.title: Ambrosia Gold
gold.intro: As a 'club' variety, Ambrosia was patented and quality-controlled. Only authorized growers could produce it.
gold.market_desc: One of Canada's most-produced varieties as of 2024
